paragraphs.title: The Warriors Who Came to David at Ziklag

easy.explanation: The passage describes warriors who came to David at Ziklag.
easy.q: To whom did the warriors in these verses come?

easy.explanation: They were Saul’s brethren of Benjamin.
easy.q: From which tribe were the bowmen mentioned?

easy.explanation: They could hurl stones and shoot arrows with a bow.
easy.q: What weapons did these bowmen use?

answers: They came to assist David in battle
medium.explanation: The verse identifies them as mighty men who helped in war.
medium.q: Why are the men called “helpers of the war”?

medium.explanation: The men were equipped to shoot arrows with bows.
medium.q: What does the phrase “armed with bows” mean in context?

answers: David’s supporters included many identified warriors
medium.explanation: The verses list many warriors by name and place of origin.
medium.q: What does the variety of names in the passage show?

answers: They were connected to Saul’s family but still came to David
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes both their connection to Saul and their support for David.
challenge.q: What is significant about some of the bowmen being “Saul’s brethren of Benjamin”?

challenge.explanation: They could shoot arrows and hurl stones accurately.
challenge.q: What ability is especially emphasized in the description of the men of Benjamin?

answers: To identify the mighty men who joined David
To show they were all related
To explain that they had no military duties
challenge.explanation: The list records the identities of David’s warriors.
challenge.q: Why does the passage provide a long list of names?

paragraphs.title: The Warriors of Gad and the Crossing of the Jordan

easy.explanation: These warriors were from the Gadites.
easy.q: From which tribe were the warriors who separated themselves to David?

easy.explanation: They crossed the Jordan in the first month.
easy.q: In which month did the men of Gad cross the Jordan?

answers: It had overflowed all its banks
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Jordan had overflowed all its banks.
easy.q: What was the condition of the Jordan when they crossed it?

answers: As mighty men and men of war
medium.explanation: They were fit for battle and skilled with weapons.
medium.q: How are the men of Gad described?

medium.explanation: The comparison highlights their courage and intimidating appearance.
medium.q: What does “their faces were like the faces of lions” suggest?

answers: They put the inhabitants of the valleys to flight
medium.explanation: They drove away the people in the valleys to the east and west.
medium.q: What happened after they crossed the Jordan?

challenge.explanation: They were swift, brave, and trained for battle.
challenge.q: What combination of qualities is shown in the description of the Gadites?

answers: The crossing was difficult and dangerous
challenge.explanation: The swollen river made the crossing a notable feat.
challenge.q: Why does crossing the Jordan when it had overflowed emphasize their bravery?

answers: They had an organized command structure
They arrived only at different times
challenge.explanation: The numbered commanders indicate order and rank.
challenge.q: What does the numbered order of the commanders suggest?

paragraphs.title: The Men of Benjamin and Judah Join David

easy.explanation: The passage says that men of Benjamin and Judah came to David.
easy.q: From which tribes did the men come to David?

answers: Whether they came peaceably or to betray him
Whether they had crossed the Jordan
easy.explanation: David asked whether they came peacefully or to betray him.
easy.q: What did David ask the newcomers?

easy.explanation: Amasai declared their allegiance and peace to David.
easy.q: Who declared the newcomers’ loyalty to David?

answers: He feared they might betray him
He wanted to send them to the Jordan
medium.explanation: David asked whether they had come to help or betray him to his enemies.
medium.q: Why did David test the intentions of the men who came to him?

answers: David would join with and trust them
David would give them military clothing
David would send them to a meeting place
medium.explanation: David expresses willingness to unite with them if they came peacefully.
medium.q: What does “mine heart shall be knit unto you” mean here?

answers: He sent them to Saul’s house
He made them captains of the band
He asked them to cross the Jordan
medium.explanation: David received them and made them captains.
medium.q: What did David do after hearing Amasai’s declaration?

answers: The situation moves from suspicion to confirmed loyalty
The situation moves from war to flight
The situation moves from joy to mourning
challenge.explanation: David begins cautiously, while Amasai responds with peace and allegiance.
challenge.q: What change occurs between David’s words and Amasai’s words?

answers: Only the Philistines were helping David
challenge.explanation: Amasai says, “thy God helpeth thee.”
challenge.q: What does Amasai’s statement emphasize about the source of David’s help?

answers: He accepted them and trusted them with responsibility
He sent them away from the camp
challenge.explanation: Giving them command positions shows acceptance and trust.
challenge.q: What does David’s appointment of the newcomers as captains reveal?

paragraphs.title: The Men of Manasseh and David’s Growing Camp

easy.explanation: The passage names men of Manasseh who came to David.
easy.q: From which tribe did some men come to David?

easy.explanation: They helped David against the band of the rovers, referring to the raiders.
easy.q: Against whom did the men of Manasseh help David?

easy.explanation: People came day by day until the camp became like the host of God.
easy.q: How is David’s camp described at the end of the passage?

answers: They feared he would turn against Saul, his master
They wanted to make him king
They feared the men of Gad
medium.explanation: The Philistine lords feared David would fall upon Saul.
medium.q: Why did the Philistines send David away from the battle against Saul?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes brave and capable fighters.
medium.q: What does “mighty men of valour” mean?

answers: New people came to help him each day
medium.explanation: The text says that people came to David day by day.
medium.q: What caused David’s camp to grow gradually?

answers: His release allowed them to join and help him
His release caused them to leave him
challenge.explanation: After David was sent away from the battle, the men of Manasseh came to him.
challenge.q: What is the connection between David’s release by the Philistines and the arrival of the men of Manasseh?

answers: The impressive size of the camp
That the camp was located at the temple
challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes that the camp had become very large.
challenge.q: What does the comparison “like the host of God” emphasize?

answers: They did not participate in battles
challenge.explanation: Their positions as captains show military rank and leadership.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the men of Manasseh being captains in the host?

paragraphs.title: The Armies Coming to Make David King at Hebron

easy.explanation: The armies came to David at Hebron.
easy.q: Where did the leaders of the armies come?

answers: To turn the kingdom of Saul to David
To fight the men of Gad
easy.explanation: They came to make David king according to the word of the LORD.
easy.q: Why did the forces come to Hebron?

easy.explanation: The passage records 6,800 armed men from Judah.
easy.q: How many men of Judah bore shield and spear?

answers: They understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do
medium.explanation: They had understanding of the times and knew what Israel should do.
medium.q: What special ability is mentioned concerning the men of Issachar?

answers: Knowing the circumstances and the proper action
medium.explanation: The phrase describes wisdom about the situation and what should be done.
medium.q: What does “understanding of the times” mean in this context?

answers: They included soldiers, leaders, priests, and wise men
medium.explanation: The list includes military forces, commanders, priests, and men of understanding.
medium.q: What does the list show about the people who came to make David king?

answers: Their connection to Saul’s house still continued
They had all already left Saul
challenge.explanation: The verse says that most of them still guarded Saul’s house.
challenge.q: What is significant about the statement that many Benjamites still kept the ward of Saul’s house?

answers: The tribes did not send equal-sized forces
Every tribe sent the same number
challenge.explanation: The recorded numbers vary from tribe to tribe.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the different numbers given for the tribes?

answers: It shows that religious leaders also supported the transfer of the kingdom
It proves they were sons of Gad
challenge.explanation: Their presence shows support for David from both military and religious leadership.
challenge.q: Why is the inclusion of Jehoiada and Zadok important?

paragraphs.title: The Men of Issachar, Zebulun, Naphtali, Dan, and Asher

easy.explanation: Zebulun provided fifty thousand men who went forth to battle.
easy.q: How many men came from Zebulun ready for battle?

easy.explanation: Naphtali had 1,000 captains and 37,000 men with shield and spear.
easy.q: How many men of Naphtali had shield and spear?

easy.explanation: The passage records 40,000 men from Asher.
easy.q: How many men came from Asher ready for battle?

answers: They were committed and ready to act wholeheartedly
medium.explanation: They were not of double heart and were expert in war.
medium.q: What is emphasized about the men of Zebulun?

answers: Without hesitation and with complete loyalty
medium.explanation: The phrase describes wholehearted commitment.
medium.q: What does “not of double heart” mean?

answers: Both are described as men ready and skilled for war
medium.explanation: Both groups are listed as expert men who went forth to battle.
medium.q: What do the men of Dan and Asher have in common in these verses?

answers: They add forces from several northern tribes
They reduce the number of David’s supporters
challenge.explanation: The verses continue the list of tribes supporting David.
challenge.q: How do these verses add to the description of support for David?

answers: David’s support included wisdom as well as military strength
challenge.explanation: Issachar represents understanding, while the other tribes provide military forces.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the combination of men with understanding and men skilled in war?

answers: Captains, weapons, and men expert in war
challenge.explanation: The verses mention captains, weapons, and organized fighting forces.
challenge.q: Which detail most clearly shows military organization among the tribes?

paragraphs.title: National Unity and Celebration in Israel

easy.explanation: The passage says they were with David three days.
easy.q: How long did the people stay with David at Hebron eating and drinking?

easy.explanation: They came with a perfect heart to make David king over all Israel.
easy.q: Why did all the men of war come to Hebron?

easy.explanation: They brought bread, meat, meal, fruit, wine, oil, oxen, and sheep.
easy.q: What did the people nearby bring to those at Hebron?

answers: Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh
medium.explanation: The passage names the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh.
medium.q: Which tribes from the other side of Jordan are mentioned?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes sincere and complete support for David.
medium.q: What does “with a perfect heart” mean?

answers: To provide a great joyful feast
To store it in Saul’s house
medium.explanation: The food was brought for the celebration and communal feast.
medium.q: Why was abundant food brought to Hebron?

answers: National unity supported his being made king
The phrase refers only to Issachar
challenge.explanation: All Israel is described as being of one heart to make David king.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between “one heart” and David’s coronation?

answers: The preparations for the feast were extensive and organized
There was no food for the people
challenge.explanation: The many animals and supplies show the large scale of the celebration.
challenge.q: What does the list of animals carrying the food suggest?

challenge.explanation: The final words say that there was joy in Israel.
challenge.q: How does the chapter end in terms of atmosphere?
